description: ILLUSTRATIVE AND NON-ACTIVATABLE (VISION v1.2 §5.2, contracts/kernel-guards.md §6). Not checked: curator playbook check and the narrow check ship in PC1, and the base task-board-default is not pinned here. Each state names its kernel class (kernel-policy/1), which the kernel guards use whatever the flow says. A project playbook that extends today's task-board flow (task-board-default, research/playbook/examples/default.playbook.json) and writes only its differences. (1) The dev flow keeps today's statuses and pins the owner's roles per status: analysis = solution-architect, development = developer, testing = tester, reviewing = reviewer. testing is the only new state; today the tester role starts in development. (2) A design-task type with its own lifecycle: analysis = product, design = designer, review = product. Every move into an agent-owned state carries spawn.owner, which the flow engine (B2) hands to the role router (B3). Role pins are workflow structure, so a change to them waits for a person's confirmation (playbook spec §2.4).

product.description: Agent role. The S4 project binding may map it to the standing product keeper session, so B3 hands it a goal instead of spawning a new run (VISION §5.3).

story.description: Difference only: stories may also hold design tasks.

test.description: Whether the work passes through testing. Set by the orchestrator or a person, never by the producer: guards read it (spec §5.2).

testing.description: New state: the tester's pass before review.

transitions.description: Same guards as today; adds the spawn of the pinned developer.
Shadows the * -> to-review expansion for development: untested work goes to review only when the test field says none.
Explicit testing success path: the tester's accepted verdict is required, so no inherited wildcard decides it.
The tester sends the work back; the orchestrator re-queues it.
Closure needs an orchestrator or a person; a run cannot close its own element.
